id_and_class.summary: Arnold Zuboff argues that there is exactly one subject of experience, instantiated wherever and whenever experience occurs, so every conscious being is you. What makes an experience ‘mine’ is its first-person immediacy, which all experience shares, and the sense of being a separate self comes only from the fact that the contents of different lives are not integrated.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: One Subject of Experience in All Conscious Beings

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Universalism is mainly a theory of personal identity. It identifies the subject with the quality of immediacy, being ‘mine-now’, that is inherent in all experience, so there is one subject wherever experience occurs.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The identity of an experience and its subject depends on a pattern and is indifferent to the medium. Differences of brain, body, place, and time do not multiply subjects.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not addressed; Zuboff ties experience to a medium-independent pattern but offers no account of how experience arises.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: We know who we are by the immediacy of our own experience, not by objective facts like a name. Zuboff reverses the usual order: the first-person character of an experience makes whatever has it me.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A single subject; experiences as concrete universals, like a novel that stays numerically one however many copies exist.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through the first-person immediacy of experience, combined with probabilistic reasoning from one's own existence.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Separate streams of experience whose contents are cut off from one another, all belonging to one subject.

mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The ‘easy game’ argument. On the usual view your existence required one particular sperm and egg in every ancestral begetting, odds Zuboff puts at one in 8 septillion for just three begettings; universalism guarantees your existence as long as any conscious being exists.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Wherever and whenever the qualitative pattern of immediate awareness occurs.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Integration explains the illusion of separateness. Because each local stream of contents is cut off from others, it falsely seems that only this experience is mine, like someone who has seen one red object and concludes redness belongs to it alone.
core_claims_and_evidence: A rational person awakening in a hotel of countless sleepers should infer that all sleepers were woken (the easy game), and the same inference applies to waking into consciousness.
In a gradual exchange of body parts with a duplicate, no single step swaps you, yet the end result does; Zuboff concludes one person has both bodies.
A person whose brain is bisected experiences both unconnected fields of awareness, and ordinary boundaries between persons are equally illusory.
Universalism explains fine-tuning: you would awaken wherever in a multiverse the conditions for conscious life happened to appear.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: probabilistic inference and thought experiments.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The standard objection counts all the people who never came to exist and invokes a selection effect: only those who exist can wonder at it. Robert Lawrence Kuhn endorses this objection, uneasily. Zuboff replies that the selection effect does not explain why it was you, not someone else, who came to exist.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Zuboff offers no process, mechanism, or substance explaining phenomenal consciousness; reducing subjects from countless to one leaves that question untouched.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Zuboff pairs universalism with functionalism, which he treats as the controlling theory of consciousness: if experience depends only on pattern, nothing about the medium can divide subjects.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since experience depends on a pattern indifferent to its medium, a machine instantiating the right pattern would be conscious, and on universalism it would be you.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since every conscious being is you, you exist as long as any experience exists anywhere, though the memories and contents of one life do not carry over.

virtual_immortality.rationale: An experience is a concrete universal that stays numerically one when instantiated again, so a faithful reproduction of the pattern would be the same experience and the same subject.
